sections.title: Cairn MVP spec
sections.summary: This spec turns prd.md into code, sets the format that `cairn plan` writes, and lists what is already built.

sections.title: Format
sections.summary: Defines the key list that starts each spec section and the rules for how PRD sections count as covered.

requirements.text: Each spec section starts with a list of keys, before any prose.
IDs in keys are written in backticks and separated by commas.
A key applies to its section and every section below it.
A PRD section is covered when it, or a section under it, appears in some Implements, Defers or Context key.
A Defers or Context key also covers the sections under the one it names.
"Under" means in the heading tree, not by ID prefix; the top heading does not namespace its children.

artifacts.name: Implements
artifacts.description: Key listing PRD section IDs; used for curves, rollup, coverage.

artifacts.name: Files
artifacts.description: Key listing paths the section will touch; a trailing / is a dir; used for plan-time gate detection.

artifacts.name: Depends on
artifacts.description: Key listing spec section IDs; used for stack order.

artifacts.name: Defers
artifacts.description: Key listing PRD section IDs left for later; used for coverage; the viewer shows them as deferred.

artifacts.name: Context
artifacts.description: Key listing PRD section IDs that need no code; used for coverage; the viewer shows no badge.

decisions.text: Coverage follows the heading tree, not ID prefix.
decisions.why: The top heading does not namespace its children, so prd.goal sits under prd.cairn-mvp.

decisions.text: Cover v1 only; presence is the one v2 piece already built and it stays.

sections.title: Package layout
sections.summary: Lists the packages, the pure-core rule, and the services the CLI uses for IO with live and test implementations.

requirements.text: Core takes plain values and does no IO.
Only the CLI touches disk, git, the database or a model, through the listed services.
The PRD's Clock service is Effect's own Clock, and tests use TestClock.
Files go through Effect's FileSystem.
Commands use effect/cli.

decisions.text: Leave out @pierre/words.
decisions.why: It renders markdown to HTML strings through WebAssembly for streaming model output, the viewer would need innerHTML for it, and it knows nothing of {#id} headings; it may suit streaming session logs later.

decisions.text: Leave out @pierre/highlights.
decisions.why: It is the WebAssembly highlighter @pierre/diffs can use instead of Shiki, but it is in beta; Shiki's JavaScript engine is the default and is enough for now.

decisions.text: Leave out a SQLite package such as better-sqlite3.
decisions.why: node:sqlite needs no native build.

decisions.text: Leave out Rete, JointJS, Cytoscape, Drawflow and LiteGraph.
decisions.why: Each owns its scene and graph state, which would put state in two places beside the Foldkit model.

decisions.text: Leave out elkjs for layout; @dagrejs/dagre (MIT) is the choice when layout stops being fixed.
decisions.why: elkjs is EPL-2.0 or GPL-3.0 and 8 MB.

decisions.text: Leave out the AI SDK (ai, @ai-sdk/anthropic, @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai).
decisions.why: It adds a second schema language and a Promise API beside Effect; effect/ai covers both kinds of model.

decisions.text: Leave out Cloudflare AI Gateway as a dependency.
decisions.why: It is a proxy, not a library; baseUrl in config lets a user route through it.

decisions.text: Leave out Workers AI.
decisions.why: Cairn runs on the user's machine, not in a Worker.

sections.title: Trace
sections.summary: Defines Trace field by field: both documents with their sections, derived tasks with commits and events, section statuses, warnings and judgments, with no positions; the viewer depends only on this schema.

requirements.text: Trace holds version, feature, baseBranch, the PRD and spec as TraceDocuments, tasks in manifest order, a status for every PRD and spec section, warnings and judgments.
A TraceDocument holds the path, the whole markdown and its TraceSections.
A TraceSection holds id, title without the {#id}, level, line, parent, human and its own plus inherited keys; keys are empty in the PRD.
A TraceTask is a ManifestTask with derived status, waiting, the effective gate, TraceCommits and sorted events.
A TraceCommit holds sha, parents, subject, files, the Cairn-Section sections and the Cairn-Session session or null.
A TraceWarning has a kind, a message, and a taskId and sha that may be null.
TraceSection is declared in the contract, not imported from core's Section.
The trace carries no positions; the viewer lays everything out.
judgments is empty until the judging work fills it.

sections.title: Detection
sections.summary: gateOf returns whether a task needs a human gate and the reasons, from tags and path patterns, and status derivation recomputes it after commits.

requirements.text: gateOf(task, sections, config, changedFiles) returns { required, reasons }.
Reason tag:human is given if any linked PRD or spec section has human: true.
Reason path:<pattern> is given for each pattern that matches a file in task.files (plan time) or in changedFiles (after commits).
The plan stores the plan-time result in humanGate.
Status derivation recomputes the gate with the files the task's commits actually changed, so a hit after commit gates a task the plan did not.

sections.title: Planner service
sections.summary: The planner makes five calls through the LanguageModel: spec, tasks, splitSection, splitTask and index, each with a prompt file and one decode retry; model and reasoning are proposals, and the model never decides gates, IDs, branch names or order.

requirements.text: The planner makes five calls, each with a prompt file in packages/cli/prompts/.
spec(prd) returns spec markdown, with this file as its worked example.
tasks(prd, spec) returns TaskDraft[] decoded through the TaskDraft schema.
Model and reasoning in a TaskDraft are proposals that routing can replace.
splitSection(section, reason) returns two or more sections under the same parent with the same Implements.
splitTask(draft, spec, reason) returns two or more TaskDrafts that together cover the draft's spec sections and files.
index(section) returns the prose fields of an IndexedSection.
A failed decode retries once with the error in the prompt, then fails with a PlannerError.
The model never decides gates, IDs, branch names or order.
The live layer uses the LanguageModel from spec.models.
The test layer replays fixtures: this spec.md, the drafts behind manifest.json, this repo's spec.json and scripted splits.

sections.title: Stack order
sections.summary: stackOf orders drafts by dependency and returns a set of stacks: parentOf puts a task on the latest of its dependencies when they share one chain, and starts it from baseBranch after they land when they do not.

requirements.text: stackOf(feature, drafts, gates) returns the tasks as a set of stacks.
Tasks are topologically sorted by dependency; among tasks whose dependencies are placed, gated ones go first, then planner order.
IDs are t1… in that order, and branches are <feature>/<NN>-<slug>.
dependsOn is the draft's dependencies, as task IDs.
A task with no dependencies has parent null and starts a stack on baseBranch.
A task whose dependencies all lie on one chain takes the latest of them as its parent.
A task whose dependencies lie on different stacks has parent null and starts from baseBranch once every dependency has landed.
A cycle fails with a PlannerError naming the tasks in it.
worktreesOf gives each task the worktree of its parent or a dependency when that worktree's latest task is one it depends on and no other task has taken it next; otherwise a new one.
The first worktree is the repo's own checkout (null); the rest are wt-1, wt-2, ….
Tasks that can run at the same time never share a worktree.

decisions.text: Every ancestor of a task is something it depends on.
decisions.why: So a gated task has nothing below it but its own dependencies, and tasks on different stacks can be built at the same time.

sections.title: `cairn plan`
sections.summary: cairn plan assigns IDs, generates or reuses the spec, drafts and orders tasks, lints in memory, confirms and writes manifest.json.

requirements.text: Assign missing IDs in prd.md.
If spec.md is missing or --respec is passed, generate it and assign its IDs; otherwise keep the human's edits.
Draft tasks.
If TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set, refine the spec and drafts; otherwise print "Judging skipped: TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not set." and keep the drafts.
Compute gates, order the stack, ask the stack questions, and lint in memory.
Print what judging changed, then the stack with lint findings and flag or unsure judgments, and ask "Write manifest.json? [y/N]".
--yes skips the question.
Refuse to write if lint has errors, or if an existing manifest has a task that is not pending.
Judgments never block the write.
Write spec.md if it was generated or split, then spec.json, manifest.json and judgments.json.

artifacts.description: Skips the Write manifest.json? question.

decisions.text: Re-planning a started stack is not supported in the MVP; it is left to v2's rebase flow.
decisions.why: Re-planning a started stack is v2's rebase flow.

sections.title: Lint
sections.summary: lint is a pure function returning findings for eleven rules, printed by a command that exits 1 on any error.

requirements.text: lint(prd, spec, manifest, config) is pure.

sections.title: Derivation
sections.summary: derive recomputes every task status from manifest, events and commits by folding events through the task machine, with warnings for anything ignored.

requirements.text: derive(manifest, sections, config, events, commits) recomputes every task from scratch each time.
Group commits by their Cairn-Task trailer; the files they change give each task's effective gate.
Sort the task's events by ts, then by status and actor, so the order of lines in the file never matters.

Fold events through the task machine: running sends start; done sends approve from blocked_on_human when the actor is human, and finish otherwise; blocked_on_human sends finish; failed sends fail; landed sends land.
Send land when the task's commits are reachable from baseBranch, or a commit on baseBranch carries the task's trailer (a squash merge).
An orchestrator that reports done for a gated task still leaves it in blocked_on_human; the machine enforces the gate, not the orchestrator.

Anything the machine ignores becomes a warning in the result, not an error: an illegal transition, an approval from a non-human actor, an event or trailer for an unknown task, a commit on a task branch without trailers, and a branch that landed without approval.
A pending task with a blocked_on_human task below it is marked waiting, so the viewer can show why it has not started.

Rule 4: landed if all have landed, done if all are done or landed, pending if all are pending.
Rule 5: in_progress otherwise.

sections.title: Orchestrator adapter
sections.summary: Lists what the existing orchestrator must do per task using only @cairn/contract/js and the CLI.

requirements.text: Read the manifest with `parseManifest`.

Take every task that is `pending` in `cairn status --json` whose dependencies are `done` or `landed`, and whose dependencies off its own chain are `landed`, and run them in parallel; how many run at once is the orchestrator's choice.

Work in the task's worktree (the repo's own checkout when null, otherwise `git worktree add ../<repo>-<worktree>` the first time), then `gt checkout` the parent branch, or `baseBranch` after `gt sync` when the task has no parent.
Call `appendEvent` with `running`.
Run the agent with a new session ID; its first commit is `gt create <branch> -m <message>` and later ones are `gt modify --commit -m <message>`, each message ending with the `formatTrailers` block.
Pipe the session log to `cairn session put`.
Call `appendEvent` with `failed`, or `blocked_on_human` when `humanGate.required`, and `done` otherwise.
A blocked task stops its chain until `cairn approve`.
The orchestrator uses only `@cairn/contract/js` and the CLI.
`gt submit --stack` opens or updates one pull request per task, and `gt sync` pulls baseBranch, deletes merged branches and restacks the rest.
Neither Cairn nor the orchestrator rebases a branch by hand; Graphite owns branches, restacking and pull requests.
Landing is read from git: a squash merge carries the task's trailers onto baseBranch.
No Graphite command runs with `--no-verify`; hooks gate every commit.

sections.title: Model and messages
sections.summary: Specifies the viewer model, its messages, the pure chainOf function and the three-column layout.

requirements.text: The model holds the trace, the hovered node, the selected node, the drawer, the measured node positions and the canvas viewport.
`chainOf(trace, node)` is pure and returns the PRD sections, spec sections and tasks linked to a node, in both directions.
Hovering highlights the chain; clicking selects it.
Layout is PRD, spec, then the stacks.
Each section heading carries its rollup badge, and each task node shows branch, model, status and a gate marker.
A spec section or task node with a flag or unsure judgment shows a judgment marker, dimmed when the judgment is stale.
The stacks area is a node graph, one column per chain, read bottom to top.
Under cairn serve, a subscription in load.ts fetches /api/trace every two seconds with If-None-Match.
A 200 is decoded through the Trace schema and sends SettledLoadTrace with the trace; a 304 sends nothing.
A network or decode error sends SettledLoadTrace with the error, and the view shows the error above the last good trace.
The demo build (vite build --mode demo) loads demo-trace.json once and never polls.
stackLayoutOf(tasks) is pure and gives each task a column and a row.

A task with no parent starts a new column; at a fork the first child by ID continues the column and each other child starts a new column right after it; columns are ordered by the ID of their first task.
A task's row is its wave: 1 with no dependencies, otherwise 1 more than its highest dependency; row 1 is at the bottom.
A parent and child are joined by a curve from the parent's top edge to the child's bottom edge; a dependency on another column is a dashed curve.

sections.title: Canvas and curves
sections.summary: Specifies the single canvas of three columns built on @xyflow/system, with measured positions, pure Bezier curves and XYPanZoom in a Foldkit Mount.

requirements.text: The three columns sit on one canvas built from `@xyflow/system`.
Foldkit renders every node and edge; the library supplies geometry and gestures, never DOM or state.
A subscription measures every `[data-section]` and `[data-task]` element on load and resize and sends `MeasuredLayout`.
Positions are in canvas coordinates so pan and zoom do not invalidate them.
`curvesOf(trace, positions)` is pure and returns one edge per link, with its path from `getBezierPath`.

PRD to spec and spec to task links run from a node's right edge to the next node's left edge; links in the stacks area run from a task's top edge to the bottom edge of the task above it, solid for a parent and dashed for a dependency on another column.
The view draws edges in one SVG layer and dims those outside the highlighted chain.
`XYPanZoom` runs in a Foldkit `Mount` on the canvas pane; its `onPanZoom` callback sends `PannedOrZoomed` with the viewport, and the model holds it.
When the model's viewport changes for another reason, such as fitting the selected chain with `getViewportForBounds`, the mount calls `syncViewport`.
`destroy` runs on unmount.
Support dragging nodes, drawing connections and automatic layout in v1.
When dragging comes, start as a small pointer handler that sends `DraggedNode`.
Use `XYDrag` and `XYHandle` only if snapping or connection drawing needs them.
When automatic layout comes, place nodes with `@dagrejs/dagre` as a pure function called from `update`.

sections.title: Presence on the canvas
sections.summary: Presence cursors move from window fractions to canvas coordinates, drawn inside the transformed canvas layer so they line up across windows with different pan and zoom.

requirements.text: A cursor is a point in canvas coordinates, converted from the pointer with toCanvas(point, viewport), built on pointToRendererPoint.
Each cursor is drawn inside the canvas's transformed layer, so it sits over the same node in every window.
A cursor label is scaled by 1 / zoom so it stays the same size on screen.
The Cursor schema keeps { x, y }; its meaning changes from window fractions to canvas coordinates.
The room machine does not clamp cursors to [0, 1].
A pointer outside the canvas pane sends no move.

sections.title: Detail panel
sections.summary: Specifies the drawer shown on clicking a section or task and the two-click path from section to commit.

requirements.text: Clicking a PRD or spec section opens the drawer with its tasks, and each task lists its commits.
Clicking a commit loads its diff.
Clicking a task shows its commits, sessions (linked to `/api/sessions/:id`), events timeline, gate reasons and judgments.
A spec section's drawer lists its judgments.
Each judgment shows its question, verdict, message and the probability or label and confidence behind it.

sections.title: Diff view
sections.summary: Specifies rendering commit diffs with @pierre/diffs parsePatchFiles and FileDiff in a Foldkit Mount, with its options and tests.

requirements.text: `ReceivedCommit` carries the patch text.
`parsePatchFiles` from `@pierre/diffs` turns the patch into `ParsedPatch`.
Cairn's code parse hunks itself; it reads the structure.
Each file renders through `@pierre/diffs`' vanilla `FileDiff` class inside a Foldkit `Mount`.
The mount calls `render({ fileDiff, containerWrapper })`, calls `setOptions` when the model changes, and calls `cleanUp()` on unmount.
`diffStyle` is `unified` in the drawer, with a toggle for `split`; the toggle is model state.
`lineDiffType` is `word-alt`, the default.
`hunkSeparators` is `line-info`, the default.
Light and dark follow `themeType: "system"`.
Files touched by a human-gated path are listed first, with the matching pattern as a label.
Line annotations through `setLineAnnotations` for review notes from `cairn.db` later.
Expanding context via `loadDiffFiles` and a route returning both versions of a file waits until someone asks.
